description: The questions a digest answers. Shipped to the browser, so the UI resolves a check's wording, section and order from here and a digest stores only an id and an outcome. Every one of the 37 built-in issue types in src/schema/ClientIssueTypes.ts is claimed by exactly one check: an issue with no home would fire and never be surfaced, which is the failure this allocation exists to prevent.

checks.question: Was received video free of recorded freezes?
checks.rule: Fails when freezeCount increases on an inbound video track, or when a track that was receiving stops entirely.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: freezeCount is absent from the platform's stats, or the counter reset inside the only interval available.

checks.question: Could the decoder keep up?
checks.rule: Fails when decode time per frame stays above the frame interval, or when the decoder stops advancing while frames arrive.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: totalDecodeTime or framesDecoded is absent, which is common on platforms that do not expose decoder timing.

checks.question: Did frame assembly or video recovery stall?
checks.rule: Fails when frames arrive but do not complete, or when keyframe recovery was requested repeatedly without a decoded keyframe following.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: pliCount or keyFramesDecoded is absent.

checks.question: Did video frames miss decode or display deadlines?
checks.rule: Fails when decoded frames are dropped rather than rendered, beyond the tolerance the rule states.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: framesRendered is absent, which is the usual case outside Chromium.

checks.question: Was the picture free of sustained compression degradation?
checks.rule: Fails when bits per pixel stays below the threshold for a sustained stretch — a picture being delivered, but coarsely.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: Frame dimensions are absent, so bits per pixel cannot be formed.

checks.question: Was received audio free of sustained concealment?
checks.rule: Fails when the concealed share of received samples stays above the threshold — audio the decoder invented because nothing arrived.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no audio track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: concealedSamples is absent, or totalSamplesReceived reset leaving no usable interval.

checks.question: Was synthesized playout excessive?
checks.rule: Fails when the jitter buffer stretched or invented playout beyond the threshold, as reported by the built-in detector and corroborated by the sample counters.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no audio track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: The inserted/removed sample counters are absent.

checks.question: Did the jitter buffer avoid sustained stress?
checks.rule: Fails when mean jitter buffer delay stays above the threshold. Delay is a ratio of sums over the interval, never a mean of per-sample delays.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no audio track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: jitterBufferEmittedCount is absent or did not advance.

checks.question: Did audio and video stay in sync?
checks.rule: Fails when the built-in detector reports a sustained audio/video presentation offset for the same remote participant.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received only one media kind, so there is nothing to be out of sync with.
checks.notAssessableWhen: Playout timing is not exposed for both tracks.

checks.question: Did capture keep up with intended output?
checks.rule: Fails when the media source delivered fewer frames than the track's intended rate for a sustained stretch.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: The media source's frame rate is absent.

checks.question: Did encoding keep up with capture?
checks.rule: Fails when encode time per frame stays above the frame interval, or when captured frames are not reaching the encoder.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no video track.
checks.notAssessableWhen: totalEncodeTime is absent.

checks.question: Was the intended microphone producing audio?
checks.rule: Fails when the audio media source reports no energy while the track is unmuted and expected to be live, or when the capture source was lost.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no audio track, or the track was muted throughout — a muted microphone is silent on purpose.
checks.notAssessableWhen: The media source's audioLevel is absent.

checks.question: Did the sender maintain expected media output?
checks.rule: Fails when an unmuted outbound track stopped producing packets, or the sender stalled while media was expected.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no media.
checks.notAssessableWhen: Outbound counters reset with no usable interval either side.

checks.question: Did the encoder report a quality limitation?
checks.rule: Fails when the outbound track reports a sustained qualityLimitationReason. This is the ENCODER'S OWN reason code — reported as `cpu`, `bandwidth` or `other` — and it is not host CPU utilisation. No browser API exposes process CPU; a page that labels this 'CPU usage' is asserting something the data cannot support.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no media.
checks.notAssessableWhen: qualityLimitationReason is absent, which is the case outside Chromium.

checks.question: Did all fresh RTCP RTT observations stay below 300 ms?
checks.rule: Fails when a fresh round-trip observation exceeds the threshold. Only fresh reports count: one stale remote report must not be counted once per local sample, which would turn a single bad reading into a sustained fault.
checks.notApplicableWhen: No peer connection reached a connected state, so there was never a path to measure.
checks.notAssessableWhen: No candidate-pair or remote-inbound report carried a round-trip time.

checks.question: Did measured inbound interval loss stay below 5%?
checks.rule: Fails when lost over (lost + received) exceeds the threshold for an interval. A ratio of sums per interval, not a mean of interval ratios: a 2% interval carrying ten packets and a 0% interval carrying ten thousand are not equal evidence.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session received no RTP.
checks.notAssessableWhen: packetsLost is absent, or both counters reset leaving no usable interval.

checks.question: Can outbound loss be reconstructed as a packet ratio?
checks.rule: An availability check, and it frequently answers not-assessable — which is the point. Outbound loss is only knowable from a remote-inbound report, and when none arrives the honest answer is that we cannot tell. Reporting 0% instead would be a claim nobody measured.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session sent no RTP.
checks.notAssessableWhen: No fresh remote-inbound RTP report arrived during the session.

checks.question: Was media delivery free of congestion findings?
checks.rule: Fails when a built-in congestion detector reports sustained congestion in either direction, corroborated by available bitrate and loss movement.
checks.notAssessableWhen: No available-bitrate estimate was reported, so a congestion report cannot be corroborated.

checks.question: Did connections remain established without interruption?
checks.rule: Fails on any interruption to an established path, or any failure to establish one: disconnection, failure, stall, DTLS failure, demux stall, a blocked direction, no viable candidate, or a path that kept changing.
checks.notApplicableWhen: The client session opened no peer connection.
checks.notAssessableWhen: No connection state history is available for the session.

checks.question: Was all relevant client time assessable?
checks.rule: Fails when assessed time is materially short of observed time: a stats collection gap, a hidden tab, or sampling that stopped before the client left. Not a quality fault — a statement about how much of the session the other checks could speak for.
checks.notAssessableWhen: Fewer than two samples arrived, so no interval exists to measure.

checks.question: Is the full call and detector assessment available?
checks.rule: Fails when a source the other checks depend on is missing: no call summary, a client session with no samples, or a monitor version whose built-in detector set differs from the one these rules were written against.
checks.notAssessableWhen: The monitor version could not be read from client metadata.
